diagnostic_evidence.quote: The $BC^1(\R)$-norm is stronger than the norm of the Wiener algebra $A(\R)$, as is implied by \eqref{eq:katz}.
The proof is based on \eqref{eq:katz} and follows the same steps as the proof in \cite[Lemma 4.2]{shi2025weighted}.

issues.failure_explanation: On R, the Wiener norm \|f\|_A = \|\hat f\|_{L^1} is not bounded by max(\|f\|_\infty, \|f'\|_\infty) with any universal c_1: the ratio is unbounded. Take \hat f = sum_{k=1}^n eps_k \hat\phi(theta - 1 - k/n) with disjoint positive bumps of unit L^1 mass and Rudin--Shapiro signs eps_k: then \|f\|_A = n, while f(x) = \phi(x) e^{ix} P(e^{ix/n}) with \|P\|_\infty \le C\sqrt n gives \|f\|_\infty = O(\sqrt n) and (by Bernstein's inequality applied to P') \|f'\|_\infty = O(\sqrt n), so \|f\|_A / max(\|f\|_\infty, \|f'\|_\infty) \ge c\sqrt n \to \infty. Even the inclusion BC^1(R) \subset A(R) fails (f \equiv 1). The valid tool is \|f\|_A \le C(\|f\|_{L^2}+\|f'\|_{L^2}) (H^1 embeds into A), which needs decay, not just L^\infty control.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the second inequality in \eqref{eq:katz} by the standard \|f\|_{A(R)} \le C(\|f\|_{L^2}+\|f'\|_{L^2}) (or a weighted-sup-norm variant) and note that the envelopes and defects are rapidly decaying on [0,T]; the downstream Wiener-norm defect bounds then follow unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The transfer of the O(eps) defect bound from BC^1 to the Wiener algebra norm in the proof of Proposition prop, and the Wiener-norm defect bound of Lemma lem:defect-wiener, are justified by a false inequality, so both proofs are incomplete as written. The conclusions themselves survive, because the relevant modulated-Fourier envelopes are smooth and rapidly decaying, for which the standard H^1 \to A(R) embedding yields the same O(eps) bounds.
issues.title: Second inequality of (2.8) [eq:katz] is false on the real line
issues.why_classification: The false display is repaired locally by a standard embedding plus a decay observation; every substantive claim and bound survives without further change.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop2 approximates the polarized solution by (a + eps b) e^{i\phi_+} up to O(eps^2), where the first-order correction b solves the linearized Schrödinger equation in \eqref{eq:ab} with source -2 c_g \partial_t\partial_\xi a and b(0,\xi)=0. For generic data this source is nonzero, so \partial_t b(0,\cdot) = (i c_g/\omega)\,\partial_t\partial_\xi a(0,\cdot) is not identically zero and \|b(t)\|_\infty \ge c t; the envelope of p therefore differs from a^+ by eps b = Theta(eps) for t>0. Dropping the eps b term as in \eqref{eq:pq} leaves an O(eps), not O(eps^2), error; the display (and the analogous line for q) is false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either replace O(eps^2) by O(eps) in \eqref{eq:pq}, or include the first-order corrections, i.e. define \wt p = (a^+ + eps b^+) e^{i\kappa\xi/\eps} e^{i\vartheta t/\eps^2} (and similarly \wt q), consistent with Proposition prop2.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed polarized approximation overstates the accuracy by one order in eps. The subsequent superposition \eqref{eq:upq} is stated with O(eps) and remains correct, and no labelled result relies on the erroneous O(eps^2) rate (the polarized error analysis uses Proposition prop2 and Remark defect-pola directly).
issues.title: The O(eps^2) rates in (2.24) [eq:pq] are only O(eps)
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and forced, and no downstream claim depends on the false rate (\eqref{eq:upq} is O(eps) regardless).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which, together with Theorem~\ref{th:MFE}, leads to the velocity error estimate in Theorem~\ref{thm}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof inserts the modulated Fourier expansion of Theorem th:MFE into the discrete velocity formulas \eqref{eq:v-pola}. The remainder R^\pm is controlled only in L^\infty (\|R^\pm\|_\infty \le C(\tau^2+h^2+\eps)), but \eqref{eq:v-pola} applies difference quotients to it, contributing O((\eps/h)\|R^+\|_\infty) and O((\eps^2/\tau)\|R^+\|_\infty). These are of the claimed order only when eps \lesssim h and eps^2 \lesssim \tau; for h \ll eps or tau \ll eps^2 (both allowed by \eqref{eq:stability}) the stated argument does not yield the bound, and the uniform-accuracy remark treats only the u-error, not the velocity. A stability estimate for \partial_\xi e (and a bound for the time difference of e), or a separate classical-regime velocity analysis, is needed and is not given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the stability framework of Lemma lem:stability to \partial_\xi e and estimate the time difference of e through the scheme (requiring one more bounded derivative of a^\pm), or restrict the velocity statements to h \gtrsim eps, tau \gtrsim eps^2 and supply the standard classical velocity error analysis in the complementary regime.
issues.overall_effect: The velocity error bounds in Theorems thm and thm:polarized are unproved in the small-mesh/small-step corner of the admissible parameter region; in the regime h \gtrsim eps, tau \gtrsim eps^2 (the paper's focus) the argument works.
issues.title: Velocity error bound not established where h << eps or tau << eps^2
issues.why_classification: The gap is closed by a routine extension of the existing stability machinery or by the same two-regime split the paper already uses for u; the claims survive unchanged in the regime of interest.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: equivalent to the norm $\|\cdot\|_{A(\mathbb{R}) \times A(\mathbb{R})}$ uniformly in $\eps,\tau,h$ subject to \eqref{eq:stability}

issues.failure_explanation: At the resonant Fourier mode theta = kappa/eps (i.e. beta - theta h = 0), the symbols reduce to \wt\gamma_\theta = 1 and \gamma_\theta = \alpha(1+\kappa^2) = \alpha\omega^2, so \wt\gamma_\theta^2/(1+\gamma_\theta^2) = 1/(1+\alpha^2\omega^4), which tends to 1 as |\alpha| = \tau/(\omega\eps^2) \to 0 -- a regime permitted by \eqref{eq:stability}, which imposes only upper bounds on |\alpha|. Hence (i) the displayed bound by mu < 1 is false; (ii) the earlier claim |\wt\gamma_\theta| < max{1,|\gamma_\theta|} fails (equality) at this mode when |\alpha|\omega^2 \le 1; (iii) \|V(\theta)^{-1}\|_2 \sim (\omega^2|\alpha|)^{-1} is not uniformly bounded; and indeed the eigenvalues \lambda^\pm = e^{i\alpha}(1 \pm i|\alpha|\omega^2)/(1+i\alpha\omega^2) coalesce as \alpha \to 0, with sup_n \|G(\kappa/\eps)^n\| \sim 1/|\alpha| (attained at t_n \approx \pi\eps^2/(2\omega) \le T), so no preserved norm uniformly equivalent to \|\cdot\|_{A\times A} exists: the lemma is false as stated. The identical coalescence at beta - theta h = 0, where |\gamma_\theta|^2 = 1+\alpha^2\omega^4, invalidates the unconditional uniform norm equivalence in Lemma lem:stability-cn, and the uniform constant in the nonlinear stability Lemma lem:stability fails for resonant initial errors.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a lower bound |\alpha| \ge \alpha_0 > 0 (equivalently tau \ge c eps^2) to the stability condition and to the hypotheses of the stability lemmas and main theorems -- then \wt\gamma^2/(1+\gamma^2) \le 1/(1+\alpha_0^2\omega^4) < 1 at theta = kappa/eps and the uniform norm equivalence holds -- and cover the complementary classical regime (tau \lesssim eps^2, h \lesssim eps) by standard leapfrog analysis, as already sketched in the uniform-accuracy remark and the \eqref{eq:initial} branch; alternatively, keep the full range and add a refined analysis showing the resonant parasitic mode is only weakly excited by the small initial error and the smooth defect.
issues.overall_effect: The linear and nonlinear stability estimates are not uniform in eps, tau, h over the full range allowed by \eqref{eq:stability}; the constants degrade like eps^2/tau as tau/eps^2 \to 0. Consequently the eps,tau,h-uniform error bounds of Theorems th:MFE, thm and thm:polarized are not established for tau \ll eps^2, which the CFL condition allows (e.g. at the paper's own switching point h^2 = c eps^5 with tau = max(h^2/4, eps h/10), where \alpha \sim eps^{3/2} \to 0). The regime tau \gtrsim eps^2, the paper's main interest, is unaffected.
issues.title: Uniform (in eps, tau, h) stability fails at the resonant Fourier mode as tau/eps^2 -> 0
issues.why_classification: The repair requires either a restriction of the stated parameter regime plus a supplementary classical-regime argument, or a contained but nontrivial refinement of the stability analysis; all advertised accuracy guarantees survive in the regime of interest, so no central result is abandoned, but the fix goes beyond a local correction.
